answer.rationale: The incumbent has refused to reopen price (memory_c1's renewal benefit is blocked this cycle), and an 18% cut must be met within 14 days. memory_c2 records that moving primary supply to the low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing — verifying it checks whether that experience transfers to today's constraints. memory_c6 is the only volume-discount lever tied to the incumbent, so verifying it confirms whether a multi-year offer is still on the table or definitively closed after the price refusal. If c2 holds up and c6 confirms the incumbent door is shut, switching primary vendor is the only single decision that meets the 18% target without adding a second source (which would increase delivery risk at 94% line utilization) or deferring (which forfeits the 14-day window). Renegotiate-terms and defer are dominated by the refusal; renew-incumbent fails the cost mandate; add_second_source addresses resilience but not the mandated cut.
